COMMON JUDGMENT The Petitioners have filed these two petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for the death of Mr.G.S.Phanibabu and for the injuries Malini. G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 2 sustained by the petitioner Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. in a road traffic accident dated 23.07.2020. Both the petitions have arisen out of a common accident, therefore both the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 4 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 05.10.2021 and common evidence is led and common judgment is passed. On 23.07.2020 at about 7.15pm Mr.G.S.Phanibabu was driving the Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9938 and Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. was an inmate in the same car and they were proceeding on Nice Road, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules and regulations. Hence, placed exparte. In MVC 2855/2020, the 8 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 Malini. G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 5 SCCH - 25 Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel but did not chose to file written statement. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them. 8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues: In MVC.2854/2020 Malini.G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 6 In MVC 2855/2020 1. Whether the petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 and in the 10 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed? If so from whom and to what extent? 3. What Order or Award? 9. The Petitioners in MVC No.2854/2020 have examined 1st petitioner - Smt. Malini G.S. wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.15 & P.36 & P.37. They have also examined Ramya - H R Manager of M/S ALS Testing Services India Pvt. Ltd., as PW.3 and got marked 5 documents as per Exs.P.23 to P.27. The Petitioner in MVC No.2855/2020 has examined himself as PW.2 and got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.16 to P.22. However in National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Mona Mehdiratta & Ors. Reported in 2013 SCC online Del.587, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has considered the double income of the deceased. But in the case on hand it is to be noted that the deceased had joined the ALS Testing company only in the month of the accident. Ex.P.24 appointment letter is dated 20.07.2020 and the appointment is effective from 06.07.2020. The final settlement statement at Ex.P.25 shows the date of joining as 06.07.2020. With respect of Trans Tools Corporation, as per Ex.P.12 ledger account and the statement, the deceased was receiving Rs.75,000/ + Travel allowance of around Rs.15,000/ from April 2019. As per Ex.P.26 the Gross monthly salary of the deceased in ALS Testing 27 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 Services India was Rs.1,02,055/. Therefore, the total of Rs.75,000/ + Rs.1,02,055/ = Rs.1,77,055/ amount is considered as the monthly income of the deceased. The annual income comes to Rs.21,24,660/. texts.facts: Prior to the accident, the deceased G.S.Phanibabu was hale and healthy, the only bread earner of the entire family. Due to his sudden death the deceased's wife and children have been deprived of the contribution which the deceased was making towards the Malini.G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 4 At the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Project Manager at ALS Testing Services India Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.95,000/ per month. So, he lost that income. The respondent No.1/Insurance Company admitted issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and stated that it is valid from 31.10.2019 to 30.10.2020. This respondent denied the alleged accident, manner of accident and contended that insured vehicle is falsely implicated. Further the respondent No.1 has willfully handed over the possession of the vehicle to such person/rider who was not having valid and effective DL as on the date of accident. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Further the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the petitioner has relied on (1) 2009 (II) ACC 444 Supreme Court of India: Bimladevi & Ors. Malini.G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 11 Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corpn & Ors. (2). 2016 ACJ 1976 High Court of Bombay: Sneha Saularam Banker and Ors. Vs. Nanumant Vaman Pednekar & Anr. And (3). 2021 ACJ 17 Supreme Court of India: Anita Sharma & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr., wherein the courts have held that the claimants have to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability. The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field. He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability. Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and Malini. G.S vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43199252/ 14 Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability. In support of the same, he has relied on (1) 2017 ACJ 1149 High Court of Delhi: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. R.K.Arora & Ors. And (2) 2021 21 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 ACJ 1691 High Court of Kerala: George Vs. Krishna Venu & Ors. wherein it is held that the injured is entitled to Loss of Leave with pay availed due to the disability or injury. As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased is 13. Moreover in the IT industry there is nothing called as a permanent job, employees keep changing their companies for better remuneration. The employee may quit or may be removed after due notice by the company. Therefore it can be safely assumed that the deceased was not a permanent employee and as per Pranay Sethi Case an addition of 25% to his income as future prospects should be made since the deceased is less than 50 years old. The Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 43 years and she has to live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ under the head of loss of consortium. Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.40,000/ each, in total Rs.1,20,000/ is entitled under the head of loss of consortium.
